headline: Anthropic's Claude skills often bend official rules for better performance
summary: An analysis of 17 official Anthropic Claude skills shows that practical implementation often deviates from documentation, especially regarding skill triggering logic and length guidelines, prioritizing performance.
details: An analysis of all 17 official Anthropic Claude skills reveals a consistent gap between their documentation and actual code. For instance, the documentation suggests skills should be under 500 lines, yet Anthropic's own docx skill is 590 lines long.

Effective skill triggering is primarily determined by the description in the frontmatter, not the skill's body. Claude tends to under-trigger skills, only consulting them for non-trivial tasks, which necessitates writing 'pushy' descriptions.

Examples from the corpus show this 'pushy' approach: the xlsx skill description states, 'Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output,' while pptx says, 'any time a .pptx is involved in any way.' This maximizes triggering rather than restricting it.

The 'under 500 lines' rule is more of a target than a strict law. The true principle behind it is the context budget; a skill's body loads on every trigger, so its size is acceptable if it holds essentials, but not if it drags along unnecessary detail.

The central skill pattern involves staged loading: metadata always in context, the body on trigger, and resources on demand. However, 11 out of 17 official skills are single SKILL.md files with no subfolders, making splitting an exception rather than the norm.

While some developers add 'NOT for X' clauses to descriptions to avoid false triggers, Anthropic's official skills almost never do. Their domains typically don't overlap, allowing them to maximize triggering without needing exclusions.

Anthropic treats skill description writing as a product, using an evaluation pipeline to measure effectiveness rather than guessing. This involves running 20 queries three times each, over a five-iteration loop, and scoring against a held-out test set.

The most valuable lesson lies in understanding the practical trade-offs that lead to these deviations. Observing how competent developers bend documented heuristics for real-world demands provides deeper insight than simply following the rules.

headline_marked: Shape-shifting mirrors on NASA’s new space telescope could [[unveil Jupiters like our own]]
headline: Shape-shifting mirrors on NASA’s new space telescope could unveil Jupiters like our own
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will be the first to use an active coronagraph, a key technology for directly imaging exoplanets.
details: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, NASA's next-generation observatory, is set to revolutionize exoplanet discovery. It will be the first space telescope equipped with an "active coronagraph" to block out the overwhelming glare of starlight.

This innovative coronagraph uses shape-shifting mirrors to precisely nullify the light from distant stars. By doing so, it creates a dark zone around the star, allowing the faint light from orbiting exoplanets to become visible.

The primary goal of this advanced imaging capability is to directly observe gas giant exoplanets. Scientists hope to find and characterize worlds similar to Jupiter within other solar systems, offering unprecedented insights into planetary formation and diversity.
